EDENOS CORE — CANONICAL ARCHITECTURE v0.1

1. LINEAGE
gardenOS Core → extract/generalize proven generic services → edenOS Core → domain/product profiles.
Do not rewrite working gardenOS simply to fit a new framework. Extract incrementally and verify gardenOS after each extraction.

2. RESPONSIBILITY BOUNDARY
edenOS Core owns generic local capabilities:
Identity; capability registry; hardware abstraction; I/O; sensors; actuators; safety supervisor; watchdog/recovery; energy; communications; configuration/storage; calibration; discovery; health; diagnostics; events; jobs; local deterministic automation; telemetry; update/rollback; security/provisioning; extension/adapters.

Optional machine capability modules extend the same architecture:
Motion; Payload/Tool; Position/Localization; Navigation interface; Home/Dock; Mission runtime.

Domain applications own domain semantics:
gardenOS owns plants, growing zones, irrigation semantics, biological/reference data and agriculture-specific strategies.
Nandi owns tiny-helper product semantics, not the universal Core.
Dedicated lineages own their mechanical/product semantics.

3. SAME CORE ARCHITECTURE
One shared architecture, multiple hardware capability envelopes. Hardware changes resources/capabilities, not the conceptual model.
Do not fork the architecture into unrelated Tiny/Robot/Air cores.

4. LOCAL-FIRST / GRACEFUL DEGRADATION
Core must remain useful without cloud, AI, Server or Companion. Machines must remain safe if communications disappear. Advanced navigation/AI may disappear while manual, deterministic automation, safety, telemetry and recovery remain.

5. AUTHORITATIVE CONTROL PATH
Commands from UI, remote, Server, AI, ROS, MAVLink or other integrations enter through adapters and Core validation/safety. Integrations do not directly own actuators or bypass safety.

6. DATA / RECOVERY
User configuration, calibration, machine identity and programs outlive firmware where schema compatibility permits. Use versioned schemas and DETECT → VALIDATE → BACKUP/STAGE → MIGRATE → VERIFY → COMMIT → ROLLBACK.

7. AUTOMATION CONTINUUM
Manual → Teach → Replay → Deterministic/Programmed → Assisted Navigation → Precision Navigation → Bounded Autonomy → Fleet Coordination.
AI is optional throughout.

8. REUSE GATE
Before implementing a subsystem:
A. Does gardenOS already implement it?
B. Can its authoritative implementation be generalized?
C. Does an established open-source/product ecosystem already solve it?
D. Can we integrate through an adapter instead of recreating it?
E. Is the capability truly universal enough for Core?
Only then create new Core functionality.
